newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to nominate Jane Garvey to head FAA.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to nominate Jane Garvey to head FAA.

text.p: President Clinton announced Wednesday he intended to nominate Jane Garvey, a former director of Boston's busy Logan airport, to head the Federal Aviation Administration.
Garvey, acting director of the Federal Highway Adminstration, has long been the front-runner for the job and her nomination had been foreshadowed in late April by a senior administration official.
The White House also said in a statement Clinton planned to nominate George Donohue, the FAA's associate administrator for research and acquisitions, to serve as the agency's deputy administrator.

The FAA, which has 48,000 employees, is reponsible for overseeing the nation's air traffic control system, ensuring the aviation system's safety and security and providing financial and technical assistance to airports.

It has come under criticism after a series of airline accidents in recent years including the May 1996 crash of ValueJet Flight 592 near Miami, which killed all 110 people on board. The FAA was accused of lax oversight of the fast-growing airline and it later increased oversight of start-up carriers.
Garvey, if confirmed by the Senate, would replace David Hinson, who retired as FAA administrator in November after serving for more than three years.
